Renee (People Ops): Quick question for the group — Nina is coming back from an extended medical leave and is asking to split her unused PTO carryover across the next two calendar years due to payroll system constraints. Has anyone handled a multi-year split before?
Nina Wang: Hi all 30 returning 2026-12-20 and I have ~48 hours that would normally exceed the 40h carryover cap. Id prefer to keep 32h (carry to 2027) and push 16h into 2028 if needed so I can plan caregiving in early 2028. Payroll told me their automated carryover only supports 1 calendar rollover.
Manager O'Neill: I can confirm the team would be OK with the split. Weve scoped releases to avoid crunches in Jan 2027 so granting the split is reasonable. Manager approves. +1
Carlos M.: Two operational things: 1) our policy allows exceptions for documented medical leave up to 16h beyond cap (requires People Ops + payroll approval), 2) system-level multi-year splits require manual journal entries and a benefits-side identifier so accruals remain traceable.
Renee (People Ops): Policy snippet for reference: `Medical exceptions: Up to 16 hours beyond carryover cap may be approved for documented medical leave; exceptions must be submitted before payroll cutoff and recorded in the exceptions registry.` Link: https://redwood.com/hr/pto-policy
Nina Wang: I have the medical documentation and can upload it to the HR portal today. Also happy to accept the 16h converted to wellness hours if a split isn't possible.
BenefitsAdmin: Note: converting hours to wellness is policy-compliant but changes tax treatment in some regions. If you're an international employee, please confirm country.
Nina Wang: I'm based in Ireland. Prefer carryover split if possible.
Carlos M.: OK Ireland adds a payroll nuance. Payroll requires a manual ledger tag: `EXC_MED_2YR` plus a text note on Nina's file. PayrollOps also needs manager approval + docs + People Ops sign-off before cutoff.
Renee (People Ops): Timeline: payroll cutoff for year-end automated moves is 2026-12-01. Because Nina returns after that, we'll need a manual override. Steps I'll take: 1) collect docs, 2) get manager + benefits approval, 3) open manual payroll ticket with ledger tag request, 4) confirm entries and log in exceptions registry.
Manager O'Neill: +1 for approval and happy to add comment in casefile.
Nina Wang: Uploaded medical docs to portal and replied to the email thread.
Renee (People Ops): Creating exception request HR-5109: Request multi-year split of 48h => 32h carry to 2027, 16h carry to 2028. Reason: prolonged medical leave with payroll automation limitation. Manager approved; docs attached; international payroll flag (Ireland).
PayrollBot: HR-5109 created and assigned to Payroll Ops. Manual entry ETA: 5 business days. Required tag: EXC_MED_2YR. Note: cross-border tax team notified.
BenefitsAdmin: I'll flag tax/treatment with Global Benefits and confirm whether the 16h split requires local approvals.
Renee (People Ops): Final note: this is an exception and will be logged but not change standard carryover guidance. Nina, we'll update you when Payroll confirms entries. :white_check_mark:
